match_same.name: Match the Same
match_same.teaches: matching identical objects and pictures one to one (the first step before sorting and counting)
match_same.representation: two columns of line-drawn pictures; draw a line to join each pair that is the same
match_same.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

odd_one_out.name: Which One Does Not Belong?
odd_one_out.teaches: identifying a set: objects that belong together because they share one attribute
odd_one_out.representation: a row of four line drawings; circle the one that is not in the set, say why
odd_one_out.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

sort_groups.name: Sort into Groups
sort_groups.teaches: sorting objects by one attribute (kind, colour, size, shape) into labelled groups, then saying the sorting rule
sort_groups.representation: picture tiles and two or three labelled sorting rings; write the letter of each tile in its ring; option: rule given or rule found
sort_groups.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

compare_size.name: Big and Small
compare_size.teaches: comparing overall size (big, bigger, small, smaller) of two or three objects
compare_size.representation: pairs of the same object drawn at different sizes; circle the bigger or the smaller
compare_size.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

capacity_early.name: Full, Empty, Holds More
capacity_early.teaches: capacity language (full, empty, half full, nearly full) and comparing how much two containers hold
capacity_early.representation: outline containers with a drawn fill line; circle full/empty or the one that holds more; option: order three
capacity_early.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

pattern_make.name: Make a Pattern
pattern_make.teaches: copying, continuing and creating repeating patterns (AB, ABB, ABC) and finding the part that repeats
pattern_make.representation: a row of boxes with a started pattern; draw or write the next shapes; option: circle the repeating unit; option: make your own
pattern_make.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

subitise.name: Say How Many Without Counting
subitise.teaches: perceptual subitising of 0-5 and conceptual subitising to 10 (seeing small groups inside a larger one: 3 and 2 make 5)
subitise.representation: standard dot, dice, finger and ten-frame patterns shown briefly on screen, printed as a grid; write the number; option: say the two parts
subitise.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

compare_shapes.name: Same and Different Shapes
compare_shapes.teaches: comparing two shapes by sides, corners and straight or curved edges
compare_shapes.representation: two shapes side by side with a same/different checklist (sides, corners, curved)
compare_shapes.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

shapes_world.name: Shapes Around Us
shapes_world.teaches: recognising 2-D and 3-D shapes in everyday objects (a clock is a circle, a tin is a cylinder)
shapes_world.representation: line drawings of everyday objects; circle or write the matching shape name from a word bank
shapes_world.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

position_map.name: Where Is It? Positions and Maps
position_map.teaches: position and direction language (on, under, next to, behind, in front, left, right, forwards, backwards), following and giving simple directions on a grid map
position_map.representation: a simple picture map on a square grid; answer where-is questions or follow arrows
position_map.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

day_order.name: First, Next, Then
day_order.teaches: sequencing events and times of day (morning, afternoon, evening, night; before, after; first, next, then)
day_order.representation: three or four picture cards; number them 1-4 in order; option: before/after questions
day_order.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

zero.name: Zero Means None
zero.teaches: zero as the count of an empty set, and writing 0
zero.representation: pictures of plates/boxes with some or no objects; write how many, including 0
zero.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

balance.name: Balanced or Not?
balance.teaches: a balance scale shows heavier, lighter or equal (balanced) mass
balance.representation: a drawn pan balance tipped or level with objects in each pan; tick heavier, lighter or balanced
balance.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

tagFixes.why: in front of, behind, next to, on top of, under (the skill does above / below / beside)
